circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281 km track designed by Hermann Tilke on Abu Dhabi's Yas Island, has served as the venue for Formula One's season finale since 2009. It represents the second of four Middle Eastern Formula One circuits, following Bahrain and preceding those in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: Albert Park Circuit, located around a lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, serves as the venue for the annual Formula One Australian Grand Prix alongside supporting racing championships. The track holds the highest FIA circuit classification and hosts multiple motorsport events throughout the year.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Styria, the 4. 326-kilometre Austrian circuit has hosted the country's Formula One grand prix across two distinct periods. Originally known as the Österreichring, it held the race annually from 1970 to 1987, before being redesigned and rebranded as the A1-Ring to accommodate the grand prix once more between 1997 and 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street racing venue in Azerbaijan's capital, positioned along Baku Boulevard with a 6. 003 km layout that ranks as the fourth-longest Formula One track. The venue first hosted the European Grand Prix in 2016 before becoming the permanent home of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards, operated by the Baku City Circuit Operation Company.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit spans 5. 412 km and has hosted the annual Formula One Bahrain Grand Prix, making it the venue for motorsport's first Middle Eastern Grand Prix event. Beyond Formula One, the track has accommodated various racing series including GP2, drag racing, and 24-hour endurance competitions, while briefly hosting Australian V8 Supercars from 2006 to 2010.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya stretches 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced design combining extended straights with diverse corner configurations, making it a versatile test for Formula One teams. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 status and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Located in the Walloon region of Belgium, Spa-Francorchamps is a 7. 004 km circuit that has been integral to Formula One racing since the sport's inaugural 1950 season. The track currently hosts the Belgian Grand Prix annually, though it notably missed the calendar in 2003 and 2006, and has maintained continuous Grand Prix status since 1985.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, Quebec, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361-kilometre track that serves as the home of Formula One's Canadian Grand Prix. Beyond its Formula One commitments, the circuit has accommodated various international racing series including world sportscar, open-wheel, and stock car competitions throughout its history.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: The Shanghai International Circuit in China's Jiading District serves as the primary venue for the Chinese Grand Prix, which took place annually from 2004 to 2019 before resuming in 2024. The track has also begun hosting the Shanghai ePrix electric racing championship since 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Silverstone, located near villages in Northamptonshire, England, is renowned as the venue for the British Grand Prix, having first hosted this event in 1948 and then staging the inaugural World Championship race in 1950. After sharing hosting duties with other circuits during the 1955-1986 period, the Grand Prix became a permanent fixture at Silverstone from 1987 onwards, which also holds the British round of the MotoGP series.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, located near Budapest in Mogyoród, became the site of Formula One's first Grand Prix held in an Eastern Bloc nation when it hosted the Hungarian Grand Prix in 1986. Built in just eight months near a major highway after the government rejected plans for a street circuit in the capital's largest park, the 4. 381 km track was constructed with remarkable speed, faster than any other Formula One venue at the time.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: The Autodromo Nazionale Monza is a 5. 793 km Italian racing facility constructed in 1922, making it mainland Europe's oldest purpose-built circuit and the venue for the Italian Grand Prix since 1949, barring a closure in 1980 for renovation. Renowned as the "Temple of Speed" for its extended straights and rapid cornering sections, the track sits near Monza in northern Italy.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807-kilometer Japanese motorsport venue operated by Honda in Mie Prefecture, hosting major international racing events including Formula One and Super Formula championships with a spectator capacity of 155,000.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street-based racing track that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, running alongside the famous Las Vegas Boulevard where the city's premier hotels and casinos are located. The layout passes by iconic Las Vegas landmarks such as the MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is a 4. 304 km circuit named after two fatal racing drivers, Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, who died in 1962 and 1971 respectively. The venue has hosted Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix intermittently, returning as a regular host from 2015 onwards on its current layout, with the event rebranded as the Mexico City Grand Prix since 2021.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary racing facility built around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens that stretches 3. 363 miles with 19 corners, allowing Formula One cars to achieve qualifying speeds averaging 139 mph. Designed by specialist circuit architects for the purpose, the track joined the Formula One calendar in 2022 as the venue for the Miami Grand Prix.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street track that winds through the Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts of Monaco, encircling the harbour area. The circuit is typically known by the "Monte Carlo" designation, reflecting that most of its layout occupies the Monte Carlo neighbourhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: This Dutch motorsport venue in the coastal dunes near Amsterdam measures 4. 259 kilometers and hosted its first Formula One race in decades when the Dutch Grand Prix was reinstated in 2021. The partnership between the circuit and Formula One will conclude following the 2026 season.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit is a Qatari racing venue situated north of Doha, spanning 5. 419 kilometers with a 1. 068-kilometer main straight.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos, a 4. 309 km circuit in São Paulo, Brazil, opened in 1940 and was renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace, who tragically died in an aviation accident eight years earlier. The track operates in a counterclockwise direction and houses a karting facility dedicated to fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street track situated along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea waterfront that has been the venue for the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since its inaugural running in 2021. The circuit also began hosting a Formula E race in 2025, establishing itself as a multi-category motorsport destination.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's waterfront district, incorporating sections of both the Downtown Core and Kallang planning areas into its layout.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: The Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya, located in Montmeló near Barcelona, spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of extended straightaways and diverse corner configurations, making it a versatile test for drivers and teams. The venue, which holds FIA Grade 1 status, accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstand facilities.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: Located in Austin, Texas, the Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile Grade 1 FIA track that serves as the permanent home of Formula One's United States Grand Prix. The venue also hosts major motorsport events including NASCAR, MotoGP's Motorcycle Grand Prix of the Americas, and the Lone Star Le Mans endurance race, while previously welcoming various other racing series including IndyCar and sports car championships.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai-British racing driver currently competing for Williams in Formula One, representing Thailand in the sport.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso currently races for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he has secured two world championships with Renault in 2005 and 2006 while accumulating 32 Grand Prix victories. Beyond his single-seater success, Alonso has achieved remarkable feats in endurance racing, including multiple victories at Le Mans and the 2018–19 World Endurance Championship, making him the sole competitor to win both Formula One and World Endurance titles.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli represents Mercedes in Formula One, having secured six race victories following his 2025 entry into the sport.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently competing for the Haas team.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabriel "Gabi" Bortoleto Oliveira currently races in Formula One for Audi. The competitor brings his motorsport expertise to the German manufacturer's Formula One programme.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finn Valtteri Bottas drives for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing over a decade of experience to the grid. He has achieved two runner-up championship finishes during his time with Mercedes and holds ten Grand Prix victories across his career.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine motorsport competitor currently racing in Formula One with the Alpine team.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Australian driver Jack Doohan holds a reserve position with Haas while racing in European endurance competition with Nielsen Racing. He made seven Formula One appearances spanning the 2024 and 2025 seasons.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The driver previously secured a victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix while competing for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar, a French-Algerian competitor, represents France in Formula One while driving for Red Bull Racing.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari who has achieved a record-tying seven world championship titles, matching Michael Schumacher's total. He also holds numerous performance records including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg races for Audi in Formula One and has achieved significant success in sports car racing, including victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans with Porsche in 2015.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand-born racing driver currently competing in Formula One with the Racing Bulls team.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a Monégasque driver, currently races for Ferrari in Formula One, where he has claimed nine race victories throughout his career. He finished as championship runner-up in 2022 while representing the Scuderia.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish driver currently competing in the World Endurance Championship with BMW through WRT, while also undertaking part-time NASCAR duties with Trackhouse Racing. The former Formula One competitor, who raced in the sport across two separate stints between 2014 and 2024, has shifted his focus to these alternative racing series.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: British driver Lando Norris claimed the 2025 Formula One World Drivers' Championship while racing for McLaren, adding to his total of 11 race victories earned over eight seasons in the sport.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Haas. The versatile competitor achieved a Grand Prix victory with Alpine at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez, known as "Checo," currently races for Cadillac in Formula One after finishing second in the 2023 drivers' championship while competing for Red Bull. Over his 15-season career, he has accumulated six Grand Prix victories.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri is an Australian Formula One driver currently racing for McLaren, having secured nine Grand Prix victories since joining the grid four seasons ago.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known by the nickname "the Honey Badger," competed in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, securing eight Grand Prix victories during his career before retiring from the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell currently races for Mercedes in Formula One, having secured seven race victories throughout his eight-year career in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz competes for Williams in Formula One, having accumulated four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American racing driver who spent two seasons competing in Formula One between 2023 and 2024. He has since transitioned to endurance racing, currently competing in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Canadian driver Lance Stroll currently races for Aston Martin in Formula One, competing at the highest level of international motorsport.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda is a Japanese driver currently working as a reserve for Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls, having competed in Formula One between 2021 and 2025.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: The Dutch racing driver has secured four consecutive Formula One world championships between 2021 and 2024 while competing for Red Bull Racing, accumulating 71 Grand Prix victories over his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu, China's sole Formula One competitor to date, raced in the series from 2022 through 2024 before transitioning to a reserve role with Cadillac. As a reserve driver for the American team, he continues his involvement with the championship while no longer competing in regular races.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: Alpine Racing represents the Enstone-based operation that Renault rebranded in 2021 to showcase its sports car marque, inheriting the French manufacturer's works team status until Renault's 2025 exit from Formula One. The squad has secured a single victory under the Alpine banner, courtesy of Esteban Ocon's triumph at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix, and currently competes with Mercedes power units.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British automotive manufacturer, has contested Formula One racing through multiple incarnations, with its current competitive entry operating under AMR GP Limited as the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker, stands as Formula One's longest-active and most accomplished team, participating in every World Championship season since the sport's inception in 1950. Known colloquially as "the Prancing Horse" after their iconic emblem, the outfit has established itself as the sport's defining institution through sustained success and continuous competition.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Haas Formula LLC is an American Formula One team founded by NASCAR team owner Gene Haas that entered the sport in 2016. The organization, currently led by team principal Ayao Komatsu, operates under American licensing and has maintained continuous competition in the championship since its inaugural season.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: This Swiss engineering firm, established in 1970, began as a sports car manufacturer before transitioning to Formula One machinery in 1993. The operation achieved significant success in endurance racing, including overall victory at Le Mans in 1989, and competed in the top-tier motorsport series for over three decades until 2025, when it was acquired by Audi to serve as the foundation for that manufacturer's F1 programme.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing operates as a British Formula One outfit headquartered in Woking, functioning as part of the larger McLaren Group corporate structure. The team has competed continuously in the sport, maintaining its base at the McLaren Technology Centre facilities in Surrey.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has competed in Formula One since 1954 as both a constructor and engine supplier, with the current team based in Brackley and operating under a German licence. The squad, officially known as Mercedes-AMG Petronas, became jointly owned by Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and team principal Toto Wolff from 2022 onwards. The marque's racing identity is historically associated with the "Silver Arrows" nickname.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that began competing in 2024, based in Faenza with a secondary facility in Milton Keynes. As one of two Red Bull-owned teams alongside Red Bull Racing, it operates as the energy drink company's second constructor in the championship.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that commenced operations in 2024 as a second outfit within Red Bull's F1 portfolio. Based in Faenza with a secondary facility in Milton Keynes, it operates alongside Red Bull Racing as one of two teams owned by the Red Bull conglomerate.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, operating under an Austrian license from its English base, emerged as a major Formula One competitor following its establishment in 2005. The team, one of two Formula One entities controlled by Red Bull GmbH, experienced two decades of leadership under Christian Horner before Laurent Mekies assumed the role in 2025.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering is a British Formula One constructor founded in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, succeeding Williams's earlier racing venture. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team currently competes as Atlassian Williams F1 Team and operates from a substantial facility in the English countryside.
